messages.subject: modelBasedQCPlots
parts:
Hello all,
I was wondering if there is a way to test the normality other than using the normal Q-Q plots, such as  shapiro.test(data) , or exploring the r^2 for example for a single protein, not just exploring the significance of a Protein from the p-value and adj.pvalue?
---------------------------
Also, say I want to explore a list of Proteins instead of which.Protein="all"
here is what i have and it worked when i manually type it in but 
dataProcessPlots(data=quantData,
                 type="QCPlot",
                 which.Protein = c("sp|A0A075B6J9|LV218_HUMAN"
                                   ,'sp|A0A075B6K2|LV312_HUMAN'
                                   ,"sp|A0A075B6K4|LV310_HUMAN"),
                 address="")

i want it to work from a list:      my_list1 <- list(data.frame$Protein)

dataProcessPlots(data=quantData,
                 type="QCPlot",
                 which.Protein = my_list1,
                 address="")

  object 'temp.name' not found

messages.author: bc13a282f8b0c08b
messages.subject: Re: modelBasedQCPlots
parts:
Hi,


then using a vector (as in your first example) is OK. To get significant proteins, do for example:
x <- <groupComparison output>$ComparisonResult
sig_prots <- unique(x[x$adj.pvalue < 0.05, "Protein"])
and pass this new vector to which.Protein



Kind regards
Mateusz

messages.subject: Re: modelBasedQCPlots
parts:
Hi,


I just ran this code:

library(MSstats)
example("modelBasedQCPlots", package = "MSstats")
unique(testResultOneComparison$ComparisonResult$Protein)
sig_prots = c("IDHC", "PMG2")
modelBasedQCPlots(data=testResultOneComparison, type="QQPlots", address="",
                  which.Protein = sig_prots)


and I didn't get that error. It just produced the qq-plots. Does that help? Please let me know if the error persists.


Kind regards
Mateusz
